To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the number of new businesses in the Czech Republic increased significantly during the 2000s, but this growth was not uniform across the regions; 2) there are several determinants of new business formation in the Czech Republic, but their importance has been changing over time, and the most important determinant is the regional level of unemployment; 3) the number of businesses in the Czech regions correlates negatively with the level of unemployment in those regions.
the Czech Republic has a relatively high rate of new firm formation.
the main determinants of the new business formation are not the same in all the regions of the Czech Republic.

the impact of the institutional and economic environment on the creation of new businesses.
